twin_fact: both nonstops scheduled at 480 minutes or 481 minutes
request: Detroit to Amsterdam overnight on February 9th for the quarterly review. Martin, my VP, approved business class. It's an eight-hour flight and I go straight from the airport into a meeting, so I'll use the arrival lounge too. Business please.

trip.purpose: Quarterly review with the Amsterdam office

must_keep.quote: International travel is to be by lowest possible airfare available. Any international travel exceeding 8 hours (whether a single segment or multiple segments combined) can be booked in an upgradeable fare or, with the prior approval of the traveler's Vice-President, in business class.
must_keep.why: the international rule: lowest fare; business over 8 hours with the Vice-President's prior approval

must_keep.quote: All airline tickets must be booked at the lowest available airfare as determined by Concur or the Travel Desk (subject to the parameters defined in this section).
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest available airfare

distractors.quote: For travelers on international flights of eight hours or greater where a business meeting occurs on the day of arrival, it is permitted to use and expense airport arrival lounges.
distractors.why: an inclusive 8-hour rule for arrival lounges, under Lodging: it does not decide the cabin

design_notes: Both nonstops are scheduled at exactly 480 minutes: not 'exceeding 8 hours' (lines 402-404), so business is not available whoever approved it; the lowest possible airfare. The arrival-lounge rule (lines 544-547) is 'eight hours or greater' and does allow the lounge, but it is a lodging rule and does not change the cabin.
